1	# SMA-860: capture a zero-argument tool-call stream for five conformance subjects
2	
3	- **Linear:** SMA-860 (follow-up of SMA-567)
4	- **Date:** 2026-11-24
5	- **Branch:** `feature/sma-860-capture-a-zero-argument-tool-call-stream-for`
6	
7	## 1. Intent
8	
9	SMA-567 added the `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` scenario to the stream conformance suite
10	(`tests/provider-stream-conformance`). Only `openai/responses` serves it. Five subjects are pinned
11	in the `UNCAPTURED` table with SMA-860 as the follow-up: `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `gemini`,
12	`litellm` and `openai/chat`.
13	
14	The suite accepts a fixture only if it meets the provenance rule (`CONTRIBUTING.md` → "Wire-format
15	fixtures"). So each of the five subjects needs a real capture before it can serve the scenario.
16	This change adds the five captures, serves the scenario from them, and removes the five rows.
17	
18	## 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals
19	
20	**Goals.**
21	
22	- G1. Each of the five subjects serves `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` from a committed CAPTURED fixture.
23	- G2. Each fixture has a provenance header that lists every edit from the raw capture.
24	- G3. The five `UNCAPTURED` rows for `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` are removed.
25	- G4. The design records what each provider actually sends for a zero-argument call. The ticket
26	  asks for this, in particular for a stream with no argument deltas and for the Gemini `null`
27	  arguments.
28	
29	**Non-goals.**
30	
31	- No change to a provider translator, unless the suite finds a conformance failure (SMA-533
32	  design §9 applies). §5 predicts that no failure occurs.
33	- No change to the `ReasoningCleanStop` rows (SMA-858) or the `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` rows
34	  (SMA-859).
35	- No new scenario. A stream with truly zero argument deltas has no capture (§4), so this change
36	  adds no scenario for it.
37	
38	**Anti-goals.**
39	
40	- A fixture that is labelled CAPTURED but has an edit that its header does not record.
41	- A script that "fixes" a capture so that it matches a sibling subject.
42	
43	## 3. Approach
44	
45	Three approaches were considered:
46	
47	- **A. Commit a fixture file and copy its payloads into `conformance.rs`.** This is the
48	  `ZERO_ARG_EVENTS` pattern of the `openai/responses` subject (SMA-567). The SMA-567 design (§6.9)
49	  requires it. The risk is drift between the copy and the file. Only review prevents it.
50	- **B. Commit a fixture file and `include_str!` it from the script.** No drift can occur. But this
51	  adds a new pattern and a frame parser for each wire format.
52	- **C. Record the capture only in the module doc** (the Gemini "Live capture" pattern). This is the
53	  weakest provenance, because doc comments usually elide values.
54	
55	**Sven picked A** on 2026-11-24.
56	
57	## 4. The captures
58	
59	Claude ran all five captures on 2026-11-24 with Sven's keys, at Sven's request. Each request
60	offered one tool, `get_current_time`, with the description "Return the current server time. Takes
61	no arguments." and the user message "What time is it?". Each request forced the tool call. The
62	exact request bodies are committed in `docs/superpowers/specs/sma-860-requests/`. Request headers
63	(keys) are not recorded.
64	
65	| Subject | Endpoint | Model | Time (UTC) | Argument deltas on the wire |
66	|---|---|---|---|---|
67	| `anthropic` | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` | `claude-haiku-5-5` | 20:38:59 | One `input_json_delta` with `partial_json: ""`. `content_block_start` carries `"input":{}`. |
68	| `openai/chat` | `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions` | `gpt-5-mini` (reported `gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07`) | 20:39:21 | The first `tool_calls` delta has `arguments: ""`. One more delta has `arguments: "{}"`. |
69	| `gemini` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-3.8-flash:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` | `gemini-3.8-flash` | 20:39:23 | No deltas. One `functionCall` part with `"args": {}`. |

71	| `litellm` | LiteLLM 1.98.0 proxy (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm@sha256:3a1980074ff2ac13883e0ffee1bebec345d8addd004be251079cee173b0e8305`), `/v1/chat/completions`, upstream `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5` | `claude-haiku-5-5` | 20:59:06 | Three `tool_calls` deltas: `""`, `""`, `"{}"`. |
72	
73	Raw sizes and SHA-256 of the bytes as received:
74	
75	| File | Bytes | SHA-256 |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| anthropic | 1364 | `b6114d956d7d80a6b315fcd2f6866fff8c776e9ebbed846c8ab7ccf9093dd86e` |
78	| openai/chat | 1618 | `5c5e74ac372aa0f954e89801c0addb62592a1ae02ad3c36b427b4d24f56d8cf2` |
79	| gemini | 1327 | `2bda3e52f91da7cbe66dac254ae8865fbd64f22a8ade1a3a7c5cf206cd2a8305` |
80	| bedrock (binary) | 1250 | `9196618e83783e261b5a3997d81a8cb343ff58bb1c560bff611a53c0d6a98b04` |
81	| litellm | 1739 | `b81bc790cdcf6a93e1ef6e8391a353a344d95549ef08a412ee0f7c1f241552c7` |
82	
83	**Findings.**
84	
85	1. **No provider sent a stream with truly zero argument deltas.** Anthropic and Bedrock send one
86	   delta with an empty string. So the accumulated arguments text is `""`, not `{}`. Gemini sends
87	   the whole call in one part. A zero-delta stream still has no capture for any subject.
88	2. **Gemini sent `"args": {}`, not a missing `args`.** The `"null"` path in
89	   `providers-gemini/src/sse.rs` did not occur in this capture. The request declared the tool with
90	   no `parameters` field at all. The capture does not show what Gemini sends for a declaration with
91	   an empty `properties` object. This change does not test that.
92	3. **LiteLLM changes the Anthropic shape.** Upstream Anthropic sends `""` (finding 1). LiteLLM
93	   emits `""`, `""` and then `"{}"`. So LiteLLM adds a `{}` that the upstream did not send.
94	4. Each capture has fields that the translators do not know, for example `caller` (Anthropic,
95	   LiteLLM), `p` padding (Bedrock), `obfuscation` (OpenAI) and `inference_geo`. The scripts keep
96	   them, because a CAPTURED payload is sent byte for byte.
97	
98	## 5. Expected suite behaviour

100	The `ToolCallsMismatch` floor (`lib.rs`, near line 1032) and assertion 10 (`check.rs`, near line
101	192) both read blank arguments as `{}`. So the `""` arguments of `anthropic` and `bedrock` match
102	the declared call `get_current_time` with `{}`. No translator change is expected. If a subject
103	fails, the builder stops, records the failure, and treats it as a SMA-533 §9 finding. The builder
104	does not edit the capture to make it pass.
105	
106	## 6. Design
107	
108	### 6.1 Fixture files
109	
110	One committed file for each subject. The raw bytes are already in the worktree at these paths
111	(untracked). The builder adds the header and leaves the payload lines unchanged.
112	
113	| Subject | Path |
114	|---|---|
115	| `anthropic` | `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic/tests/fixtures/tool_use_zero_args.txt` |
116	| `openai/chat` | `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/chat_tool_call_zero_args.txt` |
117	| `gemini` | `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/tests/fixtures/tool_call_zero_args.sse` |
118	| `litellm` | `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm/tests/fixtures/tool_call_stream_zero_args.txt` |
119	| `bedrock` | `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock/tests/fixtures/converse_stream_tool_use_zero_args.bin` (raw) and `converse_stream_tool_use_zero_args.txt` (decoded) |
120	
121	Header rules (from `CONTRIBUTING.md`, rules 1, 2 and 5):
122	
123	- Label CAPTURED. Name the endpoint, the model, the date and time, the request body file in
124	  `docs/superpowers/specs/sma-860-requests/`, and SMA-860.
125	- List Removed, Added and Changed. For the four text files the only edit is the header itself:
126	  Removed nothing, Added the `:` header lines, Changed nothing. Real ids, signatures and padding
127	  are kept verbatim. Gemini's `thoughtSignature` is kept, unlike `parallel_signed.sse`, so that no
128	  value edit exists.
129	- Give the raw byte count and SHA-256 from §4, so that a reader can check the payload lines.
130	- Bedrock: the `.bin` file is the raw capture, with no header (it has no comment syntax). The
131	  `.txt` file is a decoded view of it, with a `:` header. Each frame becomes one `event:` line (the
132	  `:event-type` header value) and one `data:` line (the payload bytes, verbatim). The header
133	  records the decode under Changed: the prelude, header encoding and CRCs are dropped, and the
134	  `:content-type` (`application/json`) and `:message-type` (`event`) headers are dropped because
135	  they are the same on all six frames. The builder writes the decode with a small throwaway
136	  script and checks that the six payloads match the `.bin` file.
137	- The header says what §4 found for this subject (the argument deltas).
138	
139	Add `*.bin binary` for the new Bedrock fixture directory to `.gitattributes`, so that git never
140	changes its bytes. (Builder's call: the existing LF rule covers only the anthropic `*.txt` files.
141	The scripts copy the payloads into consts, so line endings of the other text fixtures do not affect
142	a test.)
143	
144	### 6.2 Scripts
145	
146	In each of the five subject modules in `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs`:
147	
148	- Replace the `Outcome::Uncaptured(..)` return for `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` with a served
149	  script.
150	- Copy the capture payloads into a const, named the same as in `openai_responses`
151	  (`ZERO_ARG_EVENTS` or `ZERO_ARG_CHUNKS`, whichever matches the subject's framing). Each payload
152	  is the exact `data:` text of the fixture. Anthropic and LiteLLM payloads keep their trailing
153	  spaces inside the line.
154	- Send every frame of the capture, in order, including the Anthropic `ping` event and the
155	  `data: [DONE]` sentinel of `openai/chat` and `litellm`. Gemini ends at bare EOF, as captured;
156	  do not add the synthetic `done()`.
157	- Bedrock: encode each (event type, payload) pair with the suite's `eventstream.rs` encoder.
158	- Write the arm comment in the form of the `openai_responses` arm: the source file, the capture,
159	  and "Edits made here", which must be only framing.
160	- `request()` offers `get_current_time` for this scenario. `fixture_calls()` returns
161	  `get_current_time` with `{}`.
162	
163	### 6.3 Tables
164	
165	- Remove the five `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` rows from `UNCAPTURED` in `src/declines.rs`.
166	- Remove `Scenario::ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` from `UNCAPTURED_SCENARIOS`. No row names it any
167	  more, and a future row must again need a reviewed edit.
168	- Update the comment above the removed rows and any doc that says only `openai/responses` serves
169	  the scenario (the builder searches for `SMA-860` and "only `openai/responses`").
170	
171	### 6.4 Documentation
172	
173	- No mdBook or README change. This is a change to an unpublished test crate and to test fixtures.
174	  It changes no public API.
175	- Fixture files under `crates/*/tests/` are in the published packages (no crate sets `include` or
176	  `exclude`). So release-plz will give the five provider crates a patch bump and the facade a
177	  cascade. This is expected and harmless.
178	
179	### 6.5 Verification
180	
181	- `cargo test -p provider-stream-conformance` (use the package name from its `Cargo.toml`) passes.
182	- A negative check for each subject: change the copied arguments of the zero-argument call to
183	  `{"x":1}` and confirm the suite fails with `ToolCallsMismatch`. Then revert.
184	- The full CI gate list in `CLAUDE.md`.
185	
186	## 7. Left to the builder
187	
188	- Const names and helper functions for framing, if they follow the existing subject module.
189	- The exact header wording, inside the rules in §6.1.
190	- Whether the Bedrock decode script is kept. It is not committed, unless it is needed to verify.

  `{"x":1}` and confirm the suite fails with `ToolCallsMismatch`. Then revert.
- The full CI gate list in `CLAUDE.md`.

- Const names and helper functions for framing, if they follow the existing subject module.
- The exact header wording, inside the rules in §6.1.
- Whether the Bedrock decode script is kept. It is not committed, unless it is needed to verify.

200:## Wire-format fixtures
201-
202-A wire-format fixture is a file or test script that stands in for the bytes a provider sends. A reader must know which bytes are real and which bytes are not. Five rules apply.
203-
204-SMA-585 shows the risk. `responses_tool_call.txt` is a CAPTURED fixture, but the file ended with a `[DONE]` line that the Responses endpoint does not send. The header did not record the line.
205-
206-1. **Label.** Each fixture states its provenance. Use one of three labels: CAPTURED (name the endpoint, the model and the date), HAND-AUTHORED, or CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts.
207-2. **Edits.** A CAPTURED fixture lists every edit from the raw capture in three parts: Removed, Added and Changed. Changed covers reorders, reformats and value edits. Write "nothing" only when the record shows that a part is empty. If the raw capture is not available, write "not recorded" for a part that you cannot check, and say what evidence exists. The header of `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt` is the worked example.
208-3. **Hand-authored shapes.** A HAND-AUTHORED fixture names the source of each shape. The source is a capture or a vendored type. Do not copy framing from a different endpoint or API.
209-4. **No conformity edits.** Do not add, remove or reorder a line to make a fixture match a sibling fixture. If you must, record the edit under Changed.
210-5. **Where the header goes.** An SSE fixture or other text fixture carries a `:` comment header. A format with no comment syntax records its provenance in the doc comment of the test that loads it. An inline wire helper in test code cites its source in the same way. A synthetic addition in a test script is allowed if its doc comment says that it is not captured. The Gemini `done()` in `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs` is an example.

220-```

200:## Wire-format fixtures
201-
202-A wire-format fixture is a file or test script that stands in for the bytes a provider sends. A reader must know which bytes are real and which bytes are not. Five rules apply.
203-
204-SMA-585 shows the risk. `responses_tool_call.txt` is a CAPTURED fixture, but the file ended with a `[DONE]` line that the Responses endpoint does not send. The header did not record the line.
205-
206-1. **Label.** Each fixture states its provenance. Use one of three labels: CAPTURED (name the endpoint, the model and the date), HAND-AUTHORED, or CAPTURED with named reconstructed parts.
207-2. **Edits.** A CAPTURED fixture lists every edit from the raw capture in three parts: Removed, Added and Changed. Changed covers reorders, reformats and value edits. Write "nothing" only when the record shows that a part is empty. If the raw capture is not available, write "not recorded" for a part that you cannot check, and say what evidence exists. The header of `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-openai/tests/fixtures/responses_tool_call.txt` is the worked example.
208-3. **Hand-authored shapes.** A HAND-AUTHORED fixture names the source of each shape. The source is a capture or a vendored type. Do not copy framing from a different endpoint or API.
209-4. **No conformity edits.** Do not add, remove or reorder a line to make a fixture match a sibling fixture. If you must, record the edit under Changed.
210-5. **Where the header goes.** An SSE fixture or other text fixture carries a `:` comment header. A format with no comment syntax records its provenance in the doc comment of the test that loads it. An inline wire helper in test code cites its source in the same way. A synthetic addition in a test script is allowed if its doc comment says that it is not captured. The Gemini `done()` in `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs` is an example.
